name: DrEureka
org: University of Pennsylvania, NVIDIA and UT Austin
one_liner: Eureka's reward loop extended to sim-to-real: an LLM also proposes the simulator's randomization settings so a trained robot policy works on hardware.

loop.proposes: Reward code (as in Eureka, with safety instructions) and then domain randomization configurations from GPT-4
loop.judged_by: RL training in simulation, plus a physics-prior step (RAPP) that bounds each randomized parameter
loop.steers: Reward stage: best result feeds back into the prompt. Randomization stage: open loop, no real-world feedback

headline_result: On a real quadruped forward-locomotion test (2 m/s target, 5 m track), the best DrEureka policy reached 1.83 m/s and 5.00 m versus 1.32 m/s and 4.17 m for the human-designed setup. The robot also walked atop a real yoga ball for 15.4 seconds on average.
caveat: Only the reward stage closes a loop with simulation results, and the randomization stage is a one-shot proposal. The real-world numbers come from short hardware trials, and the yoga-ball runs are about 15 seconds, not minutes.
beyond_harness_note: The LLM designs training settings offline in simulation, and the resulting policy runs on the robot without the model.
algorithmic_authority: Physics simulation with RL training and a reward-aware physics prior

sources.title: DrEureka: Language Model Guided Sim-To-Real Transfer (RSS 2024)

verification.notes: Read the arXiv abstract (RSS 2024) and the HTML full text (first 100,000 characters). Table I values quoted directly. The paper text claims 34% faster and 20% farther; the track table gives about 39% faster and 20% farther for the best policy, so the card quotes table values and avoids the percentages. Affiliation order in the extracted text was ambiguous (UPenn, NVIDIA, UT Austin). Added in a second search pass. Org confirmed from the arXiv HTML title block (review 2026-11-03).
